notes:
PASS on the fake backend only (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level); this package is model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null), no hardware was attached and no hardware run is claimed.

WHAT IT SERVES: the card's models[0], src/retriever_src_kitchen/_scene/output/robots/panda.xml, as a configuration-only MujocoDriver in simulated mode R0. The card's entry_symbols list is empty; the model file was confirmed in the clone at the pinned commit. cap.world.step.v1 takes {ticks, action: {ctrl: [...]}}; each ctrl element is checked by the bridge against the model's actuator_ctrlrange (nine actuators: seven arm torque motors with ranges -80..80 and -12..12, and two gripper position actuators with 0..0.04 and -0.04..0, panda.xml:3-12) before data.ctrl is written, then mj_step runs ticks times. cap.world.reset.v1 restores the model defaults with mj_resetData + mj_forward. The state is the bridge's integration state (time_ms, qpos, qvel, ctrl, tick, timestep_ms, seed). The served model is fixed-base with nine joints (seven hinges and two slides). The card's other models tiago.xml and ur5e.xml, the kitchen scene files, the scripted demos and the Retriever pipeline, and the visual-only Mobile ALOHA staging are not served: one package serves one device, and the driver and fake use models[0].

WHY THIS SHAPE: the card is family-config with helper MujocoDriver, and the upstream provides MJCF assets rather than a Python device class; there is no deviation from the card. MuJoCo is not installed and cannot be installed where the gate runs (no network, no pip), so backends['fake'] is this package's stand-in mujoco module in fake.py, declared as the callable fake_mujoco; the lock names it .fake:fake_mujoco. The stand-in parses the same MJCF text for the actuator count, the per-actuator control ranges and the qpos/qvel dimensions, but its integration is a placeholder velocity proportional to each control value; it loads no mesh, texture, camera or sensor and resolves no contact, equality, tendon or actuator constraint. The fidelity gaps list every difference.

TIMESTEP: panda.xml sets no <option timestep>; the stand-in uses 2 ms, MuJoCo's library default, as a placeholder, and the fidelity timestep_ms 2.0 is that placeholder, not a verified engine default. MuJoCo itself was never imported, so no trajectory was compared with the real engine and the sim backend path was not run.

R0: the device is a simulated world with no hardware backend, and the repository documents no real-device or hardware access (README.md:104); the card risk floor and the cap.world.step.v1 and cap.world.reset.v1 class floors are R0. No independent e-stop is claimed; the runtime's software latch is the only stop.

WARNINGS (all expected, none failed): G6.NOT_RECORDED and G7.UPSTREAM_BACKEND because the fake backend is a stand-in for the mujoco module rather than a package class the gate can wrap in a Recorder; G8.NO_UNIT x3 for the bridge-derived ticks, action.ctrl[*] and seed inputs. No G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warning was raised.

TESTS: test_driver.py keeps mhs.testing.check_driver and adds six cases (model shape from the card model, per-actuator control-range refusals with zero effect, state following the control target, reset to the model defaults, published fidelity contract, e-stop latch); they pass. No catalogue_requests: only cap.world.step.v1 and cap.world.reset.v1 are used. No site-limits.example.json: no operator-required bound and no package Limit.
